name: Sautens
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village at the entrance to the Ötztal, featuring a baroque church and stunning mountain scenery.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Sautens is situated in the Imst district on a sun-drenched elevated terrace at the gateway to the Ötztal valley at an altitude of 812 metres, home to around 1,600 inhabitants. Resting west of the Ötztaler Ache river, the village directly faces the striking rock pyramid of the Acherkogel (3,007 m). Known as the Gateway to the Ötztal, Sautens maintains an authentic, tranquil village atmosphere away from busy transit routes. Thanks to its sheltered topography, it enjoys an exceptionally mild microclimate often compared to Merano, nurturing abundant fruit orchards of apples, plums, and apricots alongside around thirty artisanal schnapps distilleries.

Geschichte

The surrounding landscape was dramatically shaped around 3,000 years ago by the prehistoric Tschirgant rockslide. This geological event created the Sautner Forchet, a wild boulder-strewn terrain of limestone and dolomite overgrown by ancient pine woods. The Rhaeto-Romanic place name was first documented in 1282 when lands were granted to Stams Abbey. From the 16th century onward, abundant limestone blocks and firewood spurred a prosperous lime-burning industry; in 2004, the community reconstructed a historic lime kiln as an open-air heritage site. The neoclassical parish church of the Visitation was built between 1830 and 1831 by Josef Simon Moosbrugger, while the Gothic Old Saint Oswald Church dates from 1517.

Anreise

Reaching Sautens is very convenient. Motorists leave the Inntalautobahn A12 at the Ötztal exit and follow the B186 Ötztal valley road south for merely five kilometres before turning onto the Sautens access road. Train passengers arrive at the Ötztal-Bahnhof express rail station along the Arlberg railway. From there, regular VVT buses (line 4194) reach the village square in just eight minutes. Guests with the regional Ötztal guest card enjoy free regional public bus transport throughout the valley.

Tipps

A favourite family walk is the Zauberwald Sautens magic forest, an accessible nature trail with play areas and the Three Churches Viewpoint (Drei-Kirchen-Blick) overlooking the steeples of Sautens, Oetz, and Oetzerau. In the Forchet forest, the historical lime kiln showcases traditional artisan burning techniques. Merely two kilometres away lies Lake Piburger See, one of Tyrol's warmest mountain bathing lakes, featuring boat rentals and lakeside trails. Connoisseurs can sample award-winning fruit brandies at local craft distilleries along the Tyrolean Schnapps Route, while thrill-seekers enjoy whitewater rafting on the river or visit nearby AREA 47.
